load_dotenv()

```{python}
# Load data

# this function cleans up the weird column name formatting SQLAlchemy addes to the df when loading. 
def load_table(table_name, engine):
    df = pd.read_sql_table(table_name, engine)
    df.columns = [str(col) for col in df.columns]
    return df

dc_df = load_table("naics_518_establishments", engine)
air_df = load_table("air_quality", engine)
bus_df = load_table("business_patterns", engine)
gdp_df = load_table("gdp", engine)
inc_df = load_table("personal_income", engine)
pop_df = load_table("population", engine)
perm_df = load_table("res_construction_permits", engine)
emp_df = load_table("unemployment", engine)
county_df = load_table("us_counties", engine)
```

## Create Table for models

```{python}
# keep only 2022 (closest to when we know data center counts to be true)

df_with_years = [dc_df, air_df, bus_df, gdp_df, inc_df, pop_df, perm_df, emp_df]
dfs_only_2022 = [mlu.return_specific_year(x, 2022) for x in df_with_years]
```

```{python}
# Aggregate all industry codes per county into one summed row
dfs_only_2022[2] = dfs_only_2022[2].groupby(
    ["county_id"],
    as_index=False
    ).sum()

dfs_only_2022[2] = dfs_only_2022[2].drop(columns = ["naics_industry_code"])
```

```{python}
# Add column to county_df which indicates the presence of one or more data centers in a county
dc_df_2022 = dfs_only_2022[0]

counties_with_dc = dc_df_2022["county_id"].unique()

county_df["has_datacenter"] = county_df["county_id"].isin(counties_with_dc).astype(int)
county_df = county_df[[
    "county_id",
    "has_datacenter",
    "centroid_lon",
    "centroid_lat",
    "land_area_sqmi",
    "water_area_sqmi"
    ]]
```

```{python}
# combine all data together
mega_df = mlu.combine_dfs(county_df, dfs_only_2022[1:])
```

```{python}

per_capita_cols = [
       'tot_employee_count', 'annual_payroll', 'tot_establishment_count',
       'est<5', 'est5_9', 'est10_19', 'est20_49', 'est50_99', 'est100_249',
       'est250_499', 'est500_999', 'est>1000', 'est1000_1500', 'est1500_2500',
       'est2500_5000', 'est>5000', 'real_gdp_2017_dollars_thousands',
       'current_gdp_dollars_thousands',
       'all_permits',
       'single_family_permits', 'all_multifamily_permits',
       'multifamily_permits_2_units', 'multifamily_permits_3_4_units',
       'multifamily_permits_5_or_more_units'
]

mega_df = mlu.make_per_capita(mega_df, per_capita_cols)
```


```{python}
cols_no_crazy_outliers = mlu.column_selector(mega_df, False, -1, 20, False, False)
df_trimmed_cols = mega_df[cols_no_crazy_outliers]
df_trimmed_cols = df_trimmed_cols.dropna()
```


```{python}
X = df_trimmed_cols.drop('has_datacenter', axis=1)
y = df_trimmed_cols['has_datacenter']

scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)
```


```{python}
pca = PCA(n_components=2)
X_pca = pca.fit_transform(X_scaled)

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X_pca, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42)

model = LogisticRegression()
model.fit(X_train, y_train)

y_pred = model.predict(X_test)
```


```{python}
mlu.model_accuracy_report(model, X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test)
```


```{python}
y_numeric = pd.factorize(y)[0]

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 5))

plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.scatter(X_scaled[:, 0], X_scaled[:, 1], c=y_numeric, cmap='coolwarm', edgecolor='k', s=80)
plt.xlabel('Original Feature 1')
plt.ylabel('Original Feature 2')
plt.title('Before PCA: Using First 2 Standardized Features')
plt.colorbar(label='Target classes')

plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
plt.scatter(X_pca[:, 0], X_pca[:, 1], c=y_numeric, cmap='coolwarm', edgecolor='k', s=80)
plt.xlabel('Principal Component 1')
plt.ylabel('Principal Component 2')
plt.title('After PCA: Projected onto 2 Principal Components')
plt.colorbar(label='Target classes')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
